sections.kicker: Prepared for Espro Coffee House by Atla · November 2026
sections.lead: We looked at your Instagram the way a new customer would. Here is what stood out, in order of weight.
sections.thesis: Espro already wrote its idea. It sits in a caption, not in the bio.
sections.keep: The dark amber grid. The cups, the bar and the serif wordmark all look like the same room.

pins.what: The bio is the line every cafe writes.
pins.why: Anyone can say neighborhood and specialty coffee. It does not say why Espro and not the cafe down the road.
pins.how: Lead the bio with the idea that is already in your captions.
pins.label: Your bio
pins.cost: Customers file Espro next to every other neighborhood cafe.

pins.quote: espro is our city’s living room
pins.what: The strongest idea Espro owns lives in one caption.
pins.why: A shared living room is a reason to choose a place. It belongs in the bio, the highlights and the first post.
pins.how: Make the living room the thread and let house rules and hours sit under it.
pins.label: Your voice
pins.cost: The one line that separates Espro stays buried in a post people scroll past.

pins.area: Dark amber tones and the serif wordmark on cups, bar and posters
pins.what: Warm dark tones and a serif wordmark run through almost every tile.
pins.why: The look is already recognisable at thumbnail size, which most new cafes never reach.
pins.how: Keep it, and protect it from template posts that break the palette.
pins.label: Your grid
pins.cost: A recognisable look erodes one off-palette post at a time.

sections.intro: You asked for a look at Espro Coffee House. I spent some time on your Instagram. Three things stood out, and all three point the same way.
